investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T04:34–04:42Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered as fallback targets. Because no VM was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256 received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing). This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval-runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because no VM was allocated
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, every new pod is immediately unschedulable. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — a surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before the eval pod was admitted. No concurrent-load evidence is present in the packet, so this remains speculative.

Lower probability — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the total schedulable pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes. No node-event evidence is present in the packet.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T04:37–04:42Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable nodes for new kata peer-pod VMs — 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod times out as Unschedulable, the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, and all required evidence fields remain empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pod node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T04:34–04:42Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered as fallback targets. Because no VM was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256 received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing). This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval-runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 144s, zero evidence keys

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — this call never completed because the pod was never scheduled

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because no VM was allocated
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, every new pod is immediately unschedulable. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — a surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before the eval pod was admitted. No concurrent-load evidence is present in the packet, so this remains speculative.

Lower probability — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the total schedulable pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes. No node-event evidence is present in the packet.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads are occupying the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether stale or leaked pods are consuming capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks failed with the same Unschedulable scheduler message citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that carry this resource type (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all remote-agent scheduling pressure onto only 2 kata-capable nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; if the pod cannot be scheduled, no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails entirely (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state eval checks (required checks)
affectedAreas.reason: Both sibling checks are marked required=true (features.json line 183-184) and both failed with the same scheduling error, meaning the remote-agents feature is in a degraded or outage state per its registry thresholds (degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm resource exhaustion and identify which workloads are consuming the slots.
Check for stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs; terminate any such pods to free capacity.

Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector are intentionally excluded (e.g., they lack kata/peerpods support) or whether the affinity rules are overly restrictive and could be relaxed to increase the scheduling pool.

If kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the 2 kata-capable nodes need to be scaled up or additional kata-capable nodes need to be added to the cluster.

Monitor whether the remote-agents feature crosses the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold (features.json line 188) given that both required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) have already failed; escalate to the infrastructure team if the condition persists.
Note that remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false (features.json line 185), so its failure alone does not trigger a feature outage classification, but the two required sibling failures do.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract probe
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still active or has self-resolved; a pass would return all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and satisfy the message assertion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is consistent across the full feature and whether the feature crosses the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold defined in features.json line 188.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and current allocations
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the 2 kata-capable nodes have exhausted their vm resource slots and identifies which pods are holding capacity, proving or disproving the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect pod node affinity/selector spec for remote-agent pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms why 4 of 6 nodes are ineligible and whether the affinity rules are intentional or misconfigured, which would determine whether the effective scheduling pool can be expanded.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check for stuck or leaked remote-agent pods in the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Stale pods from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., pod spec misconfiguration, admission webhook rejection) would need to be investigated.
If a subsequent eval run succeeded and returned all 5 required evidence fields, it would indicate the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If the 4 non-kata nodes were shown to match the pod's node affinity/selector, the affinity-mismatch component of the diagnosis would be disproved and the failure would be attributable solely to kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on those nodes.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling-layer problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a cluster-node-affinity eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, alerting when the eligible node pool drops to a level that cannot absorb concurrent eval probes.

Add a leaked-pod cleanup eval that detects remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper, preventing capacity leakage from accumulating across eval runs.
Consider adding a kata-node-capacity warning threshold eval that fires before full exhaustion, giving operators time to scale capacity before scheduling failures begin.

evidenceDigest.message: pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
